I. INTRODUCTION

The direction-of-arrival (DOA) source localization

problem is directly applicable to many ﬁelds including radar,

sonar, communications, and the geological and biomedical

sciences. The goal of the DOA problem in passive sonar

applications is to accurately locate all sources with an array

of acoustic sensors. Various spectral estimation methods

have been applied to solving this problem and may be classi-

ﬁed as nonparametric, parametric, and semiparametric (see,

e.g., Ref. 1).

Nonparametric methods include the well-known delay-

and-sum (DAS) beamformer and Capon beamformer. The

DAS beamformer is a computationally efﬁcient and robust

method, but suffers in performance due to high sidelobes,

based on Gohberg–Semencul (GS) factorization is presented,

which is inspired by previous fast implementations on Capon

and amplitude and phase estimation (APES).

sensor ULAs are proposed: The computational complexity

has been reduced by exploiting the Toeplitz/block Toeplitz

matrix structure in the SPICE covariance matrix and by uti-

lizing FFT/IFFT to compute spectral estimates. In the simu-

lations, it has been shown that a signiﬁcant computational

efﬁciency increase is obtained with no loss in performance.

6  Conclusion

This study is concerned with the concept of calculating MDRSs of graphs using an integer linear programming formulation that has been proposed earlier in the literature. In this article, we theoretically establish the MDRSs for the certain families of Toeplitz graphs Tn(1,t) for t = 2, 3, 4 and n ≥ t + 2. We observed that the MD and DMD are equal for the Toeplitz graphs Tn(1,2). Also, the DMD for the Toeplitz graphs Tn(1,4) is exactly one greater than its MD. In the case of Tn(1,3), the DMD is equal to the MD for n = 5, 6, 7 and is exactly one greater than its MD for n ≥ 8. In future work, certain classes of subdivision graphs of circulant graphs Cn(1,k) will be investigated for the MDRS problem.

This research work may lead to the following open problem.

Open Problem 6.1. Investigate the minimal doubly resolving sets for the family of the generalized Toeplitz graphs Tn(1,t) for all values of t and n ≥ t + 2.

In the 𝒯 representation, the matrices that represent the operators 𝑈 and 𝜕𝜃𝑈 are not only Toeplitz matrices, but they are also lower triangular due to causality. These matrices are thus not circulant matrices, and therefore they cannot be represented by diagonal matrices in the frequency representation [Button: [38]]. However, the impulse response and its derivative with respect to 𝜃 are typically localized in time (they are equal to zero before the ballistic waves reach the output transducer, and they progressively approach zero when the waves that reach the output transducer have been scattered multiples times). Thus, for long input and output time windows, the matrices representing the operators 𝑈 and 𝜕𝜃𝑈 start to resemble circulant matrices, and thus their representations in the frequency domain become nearly diagonal. In this case the Fisher information operator becomes also nearly diagonal in the frequency representation, providing us with an alternative interpretation of the fact that maximum information states are quasimonochromatic for sufficiently long input and output time windows.

To reduce the above error sources, three algorithmic optimization strategies were further proposed. First, a sub-sampling-level synchronous gating boundary correction method was adopted. The time stamps of the IGBT switching edges were recorded on the FPGA side, and the instantaneous power values at the gating boundaries were reconstructed on the computing side using cubic interpolation, improving the effective integration boundary from sampling-point-level accuracy to sub-sampling-level accuracy. Second, the conventional discrete rectangular integration was improved by combining piecewise analytical integration with Kahan compensated summation. For each OPRM conduction run, the sinusoidal power component was analytically integrated using the steady-state voltage, current, and phase parameters, thereby avoiding integration leakage caused by sampling-point truncation. Meanwhile, compensated summation was applied during multi-run energy accumulation to reduce the propagation of floating-point rounding errors. Third, a finite-sequence bias correction coefficient was introduced into the run-length likelihood function. Since the above optimizations mainly act on the offline energy calculation and boundary correction processes, they do not change the hardware output form of the OPRM excitation signal or increase the test sequence length. The single-test duration remains approximately 49 min, with only about 0.8 s of additional computation time. Therefore, measurement-algorithm error is the main bottleneck for further improving the system accuracy, and sub-sampling boundary correction, piecewise analytical integration, and finite-sequence likelihood correction can significantly reduce this dominant uncertainty term, providing a feasible path for improving dynamic energy error measurement from the 0.15% level to within 0.1%. To further clarify the applicability of the proposed method compared with modern probabilistic and data-driven calibration methods, a comparative analysis with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and Bayesian calibration was added. In the Monte Carlo method, the errors of the steady-state power source, reference electricity meter, dynamic error test device, switching loss, measurement algorithm, and repeatability were treated as input random variables, and corresponding probability models were established according to the uncertainty evaluation results. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Direct Derivation of the Stochastic CRB of DOA Estimation for Rectilinear Sources

Article

Full-text available

  * Aug 2017
  * IEEE SIGNAL PROC LET

  * Habti Abeida
  * J.-P. Delmas

Several direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithms have been proposed to exploit the structure of rectilinear or strictly second-order noncircular signals. But until now, only the compact closed-form expressions of the corresponding deterministic Cramér Rao bound (DCRB) have been derived because it much easier to derive than the stochastic CRB (SCRB). As this latter bound is asymptotically achievable by the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator, while the DCRB is unattainable, is it important to have a compact closed-form expression for this SCRB to assess the performances of a DOA estimation algorithms for rectilinear signals. The aim of this paper is to derive this expression directly from the Slepian-Bangs formula including in particular the case of prior knowledge of uncorrelated or coherent sources. Some properties of these SCRBs are proved and numerical illustrations are given.
